column1: # Boot Bitch repair -> diagnostic invalidation map (round 30).
# THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH, consumed by BOTH GUIs:
#   - the modern Qt6 GUI (src/MainWindow.cpp; embedded at build time via
#     resources/boot-bitch.qrc as ":/data/repair-diagnostic-map.tsv"),
#   - the legacy Qt3 GUI (legacy/gui/src/EvidenceParser.cpp; staged into the
#     Etch package at /usr/share/boot-bitch-legacy/repair-diagnostic-map.tsv
#     by scripts/package-legacy.sh).
# This file serializes the round-19/20 invalidation-map table
# (Development/docs/cancel-and-cache-behavior.md section 2.4.4). A map change
# is a deliberate, reviewed edit: the parity contract
# (legacy/tests/test-ui-parity-qt3.sh) locks the row set and a golden checksum,
# so a one-sided edit (or a divergence of either GUI from this file) fails the
# gate.
# Columns: <key> TAB <requires> TAB <affected>
#   key       the tool/action row key. A key ending in ":*" is a PREFIX row
#             matching any lookup key with that prefix ("gpu:*" matches
#             "gpu:purge-wrong-driver", "kernels:*" matches
#             "kernels:remove-oldest"). Exact rows always win; the longest
#             prefix row wins among prefix matches.
#   requires  the diagnostic sections the action CONSUMES (the repair-run gate
#             + baseline serialization):
#               '-' = no baseline;
#               'report' = the combined report;
#               'union' = the union of the selected stages' requires sets
#               (plan rule rows only);
#               else a space-separated section-key list.
#   affected  the diagnostic sections RE-GENERATED after a change:
#               '-' = nothing (read-only / the proven no-op);
#               'all' = the complete set (the fail-safe rows);
#               'union' = the accumulated union of the stages' maps
#               (plan/cancelled rule rows only);
#               'shell-class' = the shell-command class row's map
#               (cancelled-shell rule row only);
#               else a space-separated section-key list.
#   A column is EITHER one reserved token ('-', 'all', 'union', 'shell-class',
#   'report') OR a list of plain section keys - never a mix. Both loaders
#   reject a malformed row fail-closed.
# Section-key vocabulary (the runnable diagnostic sections plus the
# capability pseudo-entry and the aggregate pseudo-keys):
#   environment backend package boot boot-evidence kernel grub uki display
#   gpu input network errors usage filesystem fstab btrfs mapper luks report
#   capabilities all
# 'capabilities' is the dedicated capability cache entry (cleared directly,
# never a runnable section); 'report' means the combined report; 'all' means
# the complete set.
# Code rules NOT carried as data (identical in both GUIs, fail-safe defaults
# by construction):
#   - an unknown/unclassifiable key, or a rule row ('union'/'shell-class')
#     looked up directly -> the complete set ('all'; the requires gate uses
#     the conservative 'report' default);
#   - a cancelled repair with a change  -> the union of the tool row's
#     requires and affected sets (for every real tool = the affected set);
#   - a cancelled repair with no change -> nothing;
#   - a cancelled shell with a change   -> its shell-class row;
#   - a cancelled shell with no change  -> nothing;
#   - the Full Repair plan              -> the accumulated union of the
#     selected stages' maps (capabilities included); a genuine stage failure
#     forces the complete set;
#   - a cancelled Full Repair with a change -> the accumulated per-tool union;
#   - a cancelled request with an unclassifiable verb -> the complete set;
#   - a proven no-op (unchanged|... / skipped|...) -> nothing.
# Per-distribution note (round 18/19): the invalidated KEY SET is identical on
# every backend (apt/dpkg, rpm/dnf5, apk, pacman); only the labels and evidence
# behind the section keys differ per distribution.
# The per-tool rows (the round-19 table):
validate

# Round 85: the input-device and network interactive repairs (the gpu
# pattern): the main rows consume the input/network evidence plus the kernel
# inventory and invalidate the sections their actions change; the :* rows are
# the fail-safe complete set for the sub-actions.
# Round 87: the base rows' affected sets were narrowed to the requires sets
# (input kernel / network kernel) and the include-initramfs sub-actions gained
# exact rows with the same targeted set — the include-initramfs repair rebuilds
# only the initrd/UKI images (the kernel section's initramfs evidence) and the
# input/network inclusion lines, never grub/display/filesystem/boot.  A
# completed interactive session's invalidation union (base key + sub-action
# key + the initramfs key the rebuild emits) therefore stays targeted; the :*
# rows remain the fail-safe complete set for every OTHER sub-action.
# Round 88: the include-initramfs rows' affected sets gained `usage` — the
# initramfs rebuild changes /boot contents, so the usage section's numbers
# legitimately go stale; the union regenerates input kernel usage /
# network kernel usage while the exact-row targeting stays (the user-approved
# input+kernel / network sets plus usage).
# Round 89 (ITEM 2, the stale-cache audit): every implemented interactive
# sub-action now carries its own targeted exact row (the genuinely-affected
# sections, the kernel/gpu consistency — the round-18/19 parity rule keeps
# `package backend usage capabilities` on every package-mutating row):
#   input load-module / load-controller -> input only (a live host modprobe
#     persists nothing; the loaded-modules evidence is the tool's section);
#   remove-blacklist / hid-fallback / quirk-fnmode -> input kernel (the
#     modprobe.d/config evidence + the initramfs rebuild);
#   install-package -> package backend usage capabilities input kernel (the
#     guarded package install + the rebuild);
#   network module-load / remove-blacklist -> network kernel;
#   load-candidate -> network (a live host modprobe persists nothing — the
#     input load-module pattern; round 91);
#   firmware-install / driver-switch -> package backend usage capabilities
#     network kernel.
# Round 92 (ladder steps 3-4): reinstall -> package + kernel + the tool
#   section + usage (the package reinstall and the module rebuild change
#   /boot contents, the include-initramfs precedent);
#   pin-version -> package + capabilities + the tool section (the downgrade
#   install and the preferences.d pin; no /boot rebuild).
# The :* rows now cover ONLY genuinely-unlisted future sub-actions.
input-devices
input-devices:include-initramfs
input-devices:load-module
input-devices:load-controller

# and can flip the capability evidence (the free-space gate) — the derived
# scoped set, the round-187 enable-row shape minus the package members (no
# package transaction runs).  The snapshot INVENTORY itself is re-loaded by
# the GUI through the round-135 X3 pattern, never a diagnostic section; the
# "snapshot evidence" the delete consumes is the live inventory plus the
# cached capability line (the same `-` baseline the rollback row declares).

# disk space (the usage evidence) and can flip the capability evidence (the
# free-space gate) — the same derived scoped set as the delete row (no
# package transaction runs, so no package members).  The snapshot INVENTORY
# itself is re-loaded by the GUI through the round-135 X3 pattern, never a
# diagnostic section; the create verb consumes the live inventory plus the
# cached capability line (the same `-` baseline the delete/rollback rows
